basis: Latest Operator decisions in this conversation; later decisions replace earlier conflicting proposals. Unconfirmed assistant proposals are marked separately.
graph_model: Entities are nodes; typed Relations connect them. Permitted Relation kinds constrain the valid endpoint Entity kinds.

root_entities.name: Artifact
root_entities.meaning: One governed lifecycle unit containing named dependent Entities.
root_entities.lifecycle: The Artifact has one lifecycle; its dependent Entities do not have separate lifecycles.

narrower_entities.name: Atom
narrower_entities.meaning: An Entity made of named dependent Entities, informally called sub-atoms.

root_entities.name: Scope Unit
root_entities.meaning: Organizes and owns Atoms and other Scope Units; sits outside any individual Atom.
root_entities.nesting: Recursive Scope Unit nesting is allowed.

root_entities.name: Relation
root_entities.note: Permitted Relation kinds constrain which Entity kinds may connect. Examples include Artifact to Property, Scope Unit to Atom, and Carrier to Artifact. This does not permit every Relation kind between every pair of Entities.

root_entities.name: Revision
root_entities.meaning: A historical snapshot of an Artifact.
root_entities.history_connection: Revision of an Artifact; no new native relation kind is admitted by this candidate.
root_entities.recursion_boundary: Revision is not itself an Artifact subject to another Artifact revision rule.

root_entities.name: Carrier
root_entities.meaning: What carries or stores an Entity's representation.
root_entities.placement: Separate root Entity, not a Property.

root_entities.name: Execution
root_entities.meaning: One actual run of an Operation.
root_entities.definition_boundary: The Operation definition and its actual Execution are distinct.

dependent_entities.meaning: Named Entities inside an Artifact, including Properties.
dependent_entities.property_node_vs_relation: A Property is a dependent Entity node; property-of is the relation connecting it to its owning Entity.
dependent_entities.notation_boundary: Compact examples are candidate display notation, not admission of native edges or permission to migrate Subjects.

entity_representation_rules: Each Entity instance has exactly one representation: a single source of truth for that instance.
A Projection is another Entity instance, not an additional representation of its source Entity instance.
A Projection remains derived and does not become another authority for its source facts.

representation_composition.meaning: One Atom representation may combine a folder and a file with different meanings.
representation_composition.parts_are_optional: This permission does not require every Atom to have both parts.
representation_composition.child_boundary: Carriers of child Atom instances are not additional representation parts of the parent Atom instance.

dependent_entity.meaning: Select the Atom whose Atom ID is CA-R-123, then identify its dependent status Entity. The complete expression is the dependent Entity's ID, not merely a display address.
dependent_entity.view_boundary: Resolve the owner within the selected source or Projection view; copies retaining the same source Atom ID remain separate instances.
dependent_entity.notation_boundary: The Operator's example is preserved exactly. Native identifier parsing and Subject grammar adoption are not performed.

entity_identity_model.unconfirmed_details: Path normalization, rename continuity and distinguishing multiple unnamed Actors are not specified by these answers.

atom_versioning.trigger: Every Atom update, including Status-only and other metadata-only changes, increments Version Number by 1.
atom_versioning.projection_boundary: Projected copies preserve their source Atom's Version Number; Projection rebuilds are tracked by the Projection, not by inventing a new source Atom version.

atom_lookup.default_view: Active original Atoms in the source of truth.
atom_lookup.projection_boundary: Projected instances are a separate view and do not count as additional Active original Atoms.

projection_member_model.member_instances: Derived Atom instances, not merely entries inside a Projection.
projection_member_model.whole_set: The whole set of derived Atom instances is a Projection.
projection_member_model.lifecycle: The Projection set has its own lifecycle and is managed as a whole.
projection_member_model.atom_id_rule: Each derived Atom keeps the same Atom ID as its source Atom.
projection_member_model.version_number_rule: Each derived Atom keeps its source Atom's Version Number.
projection_member_model.rebuild_tracking: The Projection tracks its own rebuilds. Its rebuild history does not increment the source Atom's Version Number.

source_reference.form: Relative link to its source Atom

projection_member_model.authority_boundary: Derived instances do not become another authoritative source for the source Atoms' facts.

draft_duplicate_policy.decision: No semantic duplicate rules for Drafts for now; their contents do not need to be deduplicated.
draft_duplicate_policy.boundary: This decision adds no Draft duplicate policy and does not change the already confirmed Atom ID rules.

relation_type_model.grouping: Relation Types have groups for Atoms, Entities, Terms and other contexts; these are not two separate Type/Kind concepts.
relation_type_model.endpoint_boundary: Grouping does not remove each Relation Type's permitted endpoint constraints.

terms_graph_boundary.decision: Terms belong to another graph, separate from the Entities Graph.
terms_graph_boundary.entity_root_boundary: This answer does not add Term as an eighth root of the Entities Graph.
terms_graph_boundary.cross_graph_links: No new cross-graph Relation is admitted by this decision.

relation_lifecycle_question.operator_context: Changing an Atom's Status is simple; checking and fixing dropped Relations can be difficult and is another task.
relation_lifecycle_question.question: Does a Relation instance follow its declaring Entity's lifecycle or have an independently managed representation and lifecycle?
relation_lifecycle_question.confirmed_choice: Keep each Relation declaration with one declaring Entity; keep Status changes separate from Relation impact checking and repair. No independent Relation lifecycle is introduced for repair work.

decision.direction: Keep an Atom Status change separate from Relation impact checking and repair.
rules: Keep one authoritative Relation declaration with one declaring Entity rather than introducing an independent Relation lifecycle solely for repair work.
A Status change is not deletion and does not itself erase Relations.
Check affected Relations against their endpoint and applicability rules as a separate task.
Report unresolved or invalid Relations explicitly rather than silently dropping them.
Require the necessary validity check before an affected Relation is relied upon.
decision.scope: The declaring Entity owns the Relation declaration; checking and repair remain separate tasks. Exact typed history links and native admission remain outside this decision.

entity_vs_syntax_rules: Syntax used to describe an Entity is not itself that Entity: indentation, headings and compact notation operators /, ., : and @.
A label or alias does not create another Entity.
A contextual grouping does not automatically create an Entity.
snapshot_and_history_rules: Entities and Properties describe the selected snapshot.
Across non-archived authoritative Atom folders combined, at most one source Atom may carry a given Atom ID.
The uniqueness boundary includes Active, Done, Backlog, Canceled and other non-archived status containers.
Derived Projection Atom instances keep their source Atom IDs and each carry a relative source link; this supersedes the earlier unqualified ban on reused IDs across every non-archived folder.
Archived snapshots may retain the same Atom ID.
Drafts remain without assigned Atom IDs.
Git preserves Atom contents and versions; Journal records changes and applicability decisions.

An Atom historical reference is Atom ID + Version Number. For another Artifact without a Version Number, it is Artifact ID + Updated At. No separate Applicable Methodology Revision or Projection Revision kind is formalized here.
Revision is a separate historical root, not an Artifact subtype or an IS_BORNE_BY child of Artifact or Atom.

history_model.journal_role: Records what happened, including changes, Executions and observed outcomes. A record is not the event itself.

version_preservation.records: Git preserves Atom contents and versions. Journal records identify Atoms involved in applicability and creation decisions without duplicating their contents.
version_preservation.storage_boundary: Every previous Atom version must remain recoverable from Git history; preserving Atom contents is not the Journal's job.
version_preservation.retention_requirement: Retain Git history containing every Atom version required for recovery. No new commit or retention mechanism is implemented by this candidate.

relation_version_binding.reconstruction_basis: Use Atom version records to reconstruct which version of one Atom was linked with which version of another Atom.
relation_version_binding.deferred_details: Exact temporal resolution and the reconstruction algorithm remain unspecified; this decision does not claim that exact historical bindings are already recoverable.

relation_proposal.status: Proposed — not Operator-confirmed or natively admitted
relation_proposal.change_record_scope: FROM_REVISION and TO_REVISION apply to records of Artifact state changes, not every Journal record. Creation has no previous Revision.
relation_proposal.execution_record_scope: RECORDS points to an Execution when the Journal record describes an actual run.

historical_reference.status: Confirmed by Operator — not yet adopted as native reference grammar
historical_reference.version_increment_policy: Every Atom update increments Version Number by 1, including Status-only and other metadata-only changes.
historical_reference.projection_resolution: Default lookup covers Active original source-of-truth Atoms, with at most one Active original per Atom ID. Projected instances belong to a separate view.

content_direction.scope_omission: Substance Scope may be omitted only for the whole governed Subject AND the whole owning Scope Unit; either restriction requires explicit Scope.
content_direction.details: General Details are optional; role/type-required content is not silently removed.

applicable_methodology.form: A one-to-one Projection of all source Atoms into status folders, not only Active; applying and manually resolving the methodology is a realization process rather than only copying a Projection.
applicable_methodology.requirement: Project every Atom from the input sources somewhere in Applicable Methodology. Keep each projected Atom mapped one-to-one to one source Atom; not every projected Atom is Active. Resolve conflicts manually rather than combining multiple sources into one derived Atom.

mapping.identity: Preserve the source Atom ID and add a relative link to that source.

registered_decisions: Which Atoms were projected to Active.
Which Atoms were projected to archived.
Which Atoms were created in Project Configuration.
decision_journal.contents_boundary: The Journal registers these decisions by Atom ID; Git preserves the Atoms themselves and their versions.
decision_journal.rebuild_roles: Source Atoms provide contents; Journal records provide applicability decisions; Git preserves recoverable Atom history. Exact record serialization and replay mechanics are not specified here.

manual_realization.conflict_resolution: Place an excluded projected Atom in Applicable Methodology's archived subfolder and record the decision in a Journal. When needed, create a new authored Atom in Project Configuration.
manual_realization.exclusion_target: The projected Atom in Applicable Methodology, not a project-local mutation of its original source Atom.
manual_realization.new_atom_origin: A newly authored original Atom may have no upstream source Atom; it is not a derived Projection member at creation.
manual_realization.subsequent_projection: That original Configuration Atom is projected one-to-one into the derived view with a link back to it.

applicable_methodology.authority: Core, Installed Extensions and Project Configuration originals remain the source of truth for Atom facts. Newly authored Configuration Atoms are original sources; Journal records register applicability and creation decisions. The derived view creates no second authoritative source for Atom facts; Git preserves Atom contents and versions.
applicable_methodology.instance_boundary: The Projection is a distinct Entity instance with one representation. References to source Atoms do not make it another representation of those source instances.
applicable_methodology.root_status: Not an additional independent root in this candidate.

m_e_root_question.decision: M and E are role-centred views over the shared roots: their specifications are Atoms; actual performances or checks are Executions.
m_e_root_question.alternative_not_selected: Add separate Method or Evaluation conceptual roots.

unresolved: Serialization and replay mechanics of Journal applicability and creation records, Projection rebuild metadata, and Git version-recovery mechanics; the Journal/Git responsibility split is confirmed.

Path normalization and rename continuity for path-based identities; distinguishing multiple unnamed Actors. Dependent Entity identity is confirmed as owner selector + dependent field; native parsing remains implementation work.
Exact typed links between Operations definitions, Executions, Actors, Journal Records, Revisions and Carriers.
A complete mapping from the captured 706-identity review to this simplified candidate.
Operator confirmation of the proposed history links; serialization of the confirmed historical-reference keys and accepted Subject grammar changes.
